newsitem.title: FRANCE: French pension fund welcomed by bourse association.
newsitem.headline: French pension fund welcomed by bourse association.

text.p: France's stock market association (SBF) welcomed the National Assembly's adoption on Friday of a bill introducing private pension funds in France, saying this would generate big flows of investment into French shares.
"This is very good news for the Paris bourse," said an SBF spokesman. "There will be a natural flow of investment into shares, which offer higher long-term returns."
French shares would attract some of the possibly 30 to 40 billion francs in total investment flows, he said.

The text adopted by the National Assembly allows for income tax write-offs for contributors capped at five percent of gross salary and also for lump sum payouts of 20 percent of pension money with a limit of 100,000 francs and the rest payable in annuities.

The funds, which would be managed by banks and insurers and set up by joint agreement between employers and employees, will be able to invest a maximum of 65 percent in bonds, leaving the way open for hefty investment in equities.
